transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... I have this issue with elevators. I mean, I know they aren't really dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I just get so scared. It feels like I'm going to be trapped in there, and I just can't make myself feel normal about it.
Is your fear limited to elevators, or do you experience similar anxiety in other situations as well?

No, it's pretty much just elevators. I don't really have a problem with anything else... like, small spaces in general don't bother me. I work in construction, so I'm in tight spots all the time, and it's fine. It's just elevators specifically.
When you're in an elevator, does your anxiety get worse if it's crowded or if you're going up a lot of floors where you can't easily get out?

I'm not really sure... I haven't really noticed if that makes a difference. It's kind of just the elevator itself. Like, as soon as those doors close, I get that same scared feeling. It doesn't really seem to matter if there's a bunch of people in there with me or if we're going up two floors or ten. It's just being in the elevator at all that does it.
Have you ever had a sudden, intense episode of fear or discomfort while in an elevator, where you felt like you were having a panic attack?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I get really nervous and I hate being in there, but I wouldn't call it a full-blown panic attack. I don't feel like I'm going to pass out or lose control or anything like that. It's just... I just get really scared and want the doors to open so I can get out. But no, I haven't had an intense episode like what you're talking about.
Do you avoid elevators or try not to use them because you’re worried something bad like a panic attack might happen while you’re inside?

Well, it's not really about worrying I'll have a panic attack, since I don't really get those. I just avoid them because of how scared they make me. Most days I just take the stairs, whether it's at our apartment or on the job sites. If an elevator or a lift is the only way up... I'll either ask for different work, or I'll only ride it if somebody I trust is standing right there with me.
Have you ever experienced physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or shortness of breath specifically while in an elevator?

Yeah, I do get some of that. Like, as soon as those doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight. My hands get sweaty, too. And honestly, all I can think in that moment is just... I need out. It doesn't matter if we're only going up a few floors, it just hits me right away.
Do you start feeling anxious even before you get into the elevator—like when you're just thinking about having to use one or when you're waiting for it to arrive?

No, not really. I don't get worked up just thinking about it or standing in the hallway waiting for the doors to open. It's really just the actual being inside part. Like I said, once I have to step in and those doors start to shut, that's when it hits me. But beforehand? No, I'm usually fine.
Have you ever felt this same way—like your chest gets tight and your hands get sweaty—in any other situations besides being inside an elevator?
No, not really. It's just elevators. I don't get that tight chest or sweaty hands anywhere else. It's only when I'm stuck in one of those things.
Do you ever feel anxious when you know you’ll have to use an elevator soon, even if you’re not inside one yet—like when you’re walking toward it or thinking about needing to take one?

No, like I was saying before, it doesn't really bother me until I'm actually in it. Walking up to it or just knowing I have to take it... I don't really feel anything then. It's really just when I'm inside and those doors close.
When you're approaching an elevator or seeing one that you know you'll have to use, do you start feeling anxious or uncomfortable even before stepping inside?

No, I really don't. Like I was just saying a minute ago, seeing it or walking up to it doesn't bother me at all. I don't get nervous beforehand. It's literally just the part where I step inside and the doors actually close. Before that, I feel totally fine.
Have you ever experienced a panic attack or sudden intense anxiety in any other situations outside of being in an elevator?
No, I haven't. It's really just the elevators. I don't get panic attacks or anything like that anywhere else. Just... when I'm in an elevator.
Do you ever feel anxious or uncomfortable when you see an elevator or approach one, even if you haven't stepped inside yet?
I... didn't you just ask me that? But no, my answer is still the same. I don't feel anything just looking at it or walking toward it. It really is just when I get inside.
Do you ever feel anxious when you’re reminded of elevators, like seeing a picture of one or hearing a story about someone getting stuck in an elevator?

No, pictures don't bother me at all. It's just a picture, you know? And if someone tells a story about getting stuck... I mean, it sounds like a bad time, but it doesn't make me feel anxious or anything just hearing about it. It really is only when I'm physically standing inside one and those doors shut.
Has your fear always been limited only to elevators, or has it ever spread to other similar situations, like escalators, small rooms, or other enclosed spaces?

No, it's really just elevators. I don't have any problems with escalators, or small rooms, or anything like that. I can be in a tiny closet or a crowded subway car and feel completely fine. It's literally just elevators.
Has there ever been a time when you were in an elevator and didn't feel that fear, or does it happen every single time without exception?

No, it happens every single time. It doesn't matter if I'm just going up one floor or ten. As soon as those doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight and my hands start sweating. All I can think is, 'I need out.' It's immediate, every time.
